entries.title: Surgeon having lunch near Krakow shooting undoubtedly saved officer's life, colleague says
entries.snippet: Further details have emerged about two police officers hailed for preventing a Polish gunman from killing more.

entries.title: Seven dead and more than 100 injured after trains collide in Egypt
entries.snippet: Several carriages derailed after two trains travelling in the same direction crashed outside the city of Giza.

entries.title: Homes and temples glow across India to mark Diwali
entries.snippet: Millions of Indians are marking the festival of lights with glowing lamps, fireworks and traditional sweets.

entries.title: Iran executes three men for 'armed unrest' after January protests
entries.snippet: It is claimed Hassan Dioband, Hamid Kazemi and Reza Zanganeh were part of anti-government protests earlier this year.

entries.title: Aramco Tower hit in heart of Saudi capital as Houthis launch fresh strikes
entries.snippet: Footage authenticated by BBC Verify shows damage to the building in the capital's central financial district.

entries.title: 'Flat', 'tired', 'cynical': Unusually gloomy Kiwis deliver New Zealand's tightest election in years
entries.snippet: The national mood is low, and faith in politics even lower - with voters deserting the major parties at the polls.

entries.title: Paraguay's former president charged after bank collapse
entries.snippet: Santiago Peña was ousted due to a banking crisis which left millions of people unable to access their money.

entries.title: Pope in 'pretty good health' as he starts Latin America tour
entries.snippet: Pope Leo travels to Uruguay just three weeks after having surgery for lung cancer.

entries.title: Italian foreign minister says hackers leaked his personal data
entries.snippet: Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni has blamed pro-Russian hackers for publishing the details online.

entries.title: Russian strikes wound nine and damage Ukraine's power network ahead of talks
entries.snippet: The attacks come before Ukrainian and Russian delegations are due to take part in trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi next week.

entries.title: US offers $20m reward for information about Iran's nuclear programme
entries.snippet: Donald Trump has repeatedly raised the prospect of renewing strikes against Iran's nuclear facilities.

entries.title: Meghan's father Thomas Markle under house arrest after child sex abuse material charge
entries.snippet: The 82-year-old appeared in court in Florida after the FBI searched two Los Angeles-area storage units he rented.

entries.title: UK cannot 'cherry pick' EU single market deal, Barnier tells BBC
entries.snippet: The former Brexit negotiator says EU countries would reject any British attempts to follow economic rules "a la carte".

entries.title: Texas mayor instructs police to limit co-operation with ICE
entries.snippet: There has been months of public outcry in Houston after an Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officer fatally shot a man who was driving to work.

entries.title: AI stocks climb after trillions wiped from market values
entries.snippet: Investors had been selling off tech shares in part due to concerns the Democrat election victory would mean slower AI development.

entries.title: New wave of bomb threats hit European airlines
entries.snippet: No link has been established between the threats against the airlines and those against the media outlets.

entries.title: Spain's rail authorities face European fraud probe after Urda rail disaster
entries.snippet: Prosecutors begin investigating EU funds meant for upgrading the Spanish railway line where a train crash killed 69 people.

entries.title: Kenyan doomsday cult leader given life sentence for murdering 191 people
entries.snippet: Paul Mackenzie ordered his followers to starve their children to death in a forest so they could "meet Jesus".

entries.title: Doctor who treated victims of Krakow shooting speaks to the BBC
entries.snippet: Two doctors were eating near the city's Main Market Square when a gunman began firing at random.

entries.title: Footage shows derailed carriages after fatal train crash in Egypt
entries.snippet: At least seven people died when two trains collided, causing several carriages to derail and fall down an embankment.

entries.title: Nvidia launches investigation into CEO's alleged relationship with Chinese spy
entries.snippet: The chipmaking giant says it is looking into reports by The New York Times that its CEO, Jensen Huang, was the target of a Chinese intelligence operation.

entries.title: NASA is looking for astronauts to live and work on the Moon
entries.snippet: NASA needs more recruits in order to return to the moon after being gone more than half a century.

entries.title: Europe to join U.S.-brokered Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi, defying Kremlin objections
entries.snippet: France says European officials will attend this week's U.S.-mediated Russia-Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi, the first three-way round of negotiations since February.

entries.title: No clear winner in New Zealand election, as leaders prepare for weeks of talks
entries.snippet: Prime Minister Christopher Luxon, who will lead a caretaker government while negotiations take place, said: "I think everyone's over politics so let's all have a bit of a break for the next three weeks".

entries.title: After a successful trip to Uruguay, Pope Leo heads to Argentina
entries.snippet: On Sunday, tens of thousands packed the main square in Florida, Uruguay, to watch Pope Leo speak.

entries.title: Russell Brand to learn sentence after being found guilty of rape and sexual assault
entries.snippet: Comedian Brand faces a "significant" prison sentence, which a London court judge is set to hand down on Monday.

entries.title: SS United States, a historic ship will be sunk to create an artificial reef
entries.snippet: NPR's Ayesha Rascoe talks to Alex Fogg, Natural Resources Chief of Okaloosa County, Florida, about efforts to deliberately sink the SS United States and create an artificial reef in its wreckage.

entries.title: Climate change is altering the colors we see in the world: an illustrated journey
entries.snippet: From Arctic landscapes to insect bodies, climate change is shifting the familiar colors of nature.

entries.title: One air ambulance service rethinks what it takes to practice medicine in the sky
entries.snippet: Air medical service comes with high risks, high costs, and staffing struggles. To reduce turnover and serve rural patients, LifeFlight of Maine is putting the needs of healthcare workers first.

entries.title: A desert stirs to life: Chile's Atacama erupts in its biggest floral display in decades
entries.snippet: El Niño rains have transformed Chile's Atacama Desert into a spectacular sea of color, awakening a fleeting ecosystem of flowers and wildlife in one of the driest places on Earth.

entries.title: Pope Leo arrives in Argentina and tells Milei that people, not the economy, should come first
entries.snippet: Leo's visit to Argentina is by far the most politically delicate of his three-nation South American tour, and a place where Leo will also confront the complicated legacy of Argentine Pope Francis, who never returned home during his 12-year pontificate.

entries.title: Voters demanded economic relief. Trump and Democrats face tough choices on how to deliver
entries.snippet: Trump, who campaigned on the idea that a Democratic victory in the midterms would trigger a 1929-style economic depression, has maintained that the economy is booming. Since his party lost in Tuesday's voting, he has claimed he is willing to work with Democrats in the House and S

entries.title: Native American women made history in tribal, state and federal elections
entries.snippet: Peggy Flanagan became the first Native American woman elected to the Senate, Deb Haaland the first to win a state governorship, and Crystalyne Curley the first to lead the Navajo Nation.

entries.title: Trump and his Justice Department stand defiant as Democrats ready an investigative blitz
entries.snippet: Trump set the tone, declaring on social media that investigative requests already made by Democrats are "extortion at the highest level, and they should be held accountable."

entries.title: The Kremlin hopes the U.S. election shake-up won't shift Trump's negotiations on Ukraine
entries.snippet: Asked if the election's outcome could stymie U.S. attempts to help negotiate a settlement between Moscow and Kyiv, Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov voiced hope that President Donald Trump will continue to pursue his peace efforts.

entries.title: Poles mourn rare mass killing as authorities say attacker had far-right views
entries.snippet: The attack, which Poland's defense minister described as an "act of terror," happened on Saturday in the Main Square, in the heart of Krakow's Old Town. The square is a major tourist hub in the country's second-largest city.

entries.title: The midterms energized a powerful political constituency: abuse survivors
entries.snippet: From Ohio Gov.-elect Amy Acton's victory to candidates accused of abuse withdrawing, advocates are calling this year's elections "a win for survivors."

entries.title: AP sources: Staff at U.S. center for AI safety are reporting to the White House, raising independence concerns
entries.snippet: Officials with the Center for Advancing Innovation and Standards for Super Intelligence, or CAISSI, an independent division of the Commerce Department, recently were asked to informally report to an office of the White House.

entries.title: Collision between 2 trains in Egypt kills 7 and injures at least 125
entries.snippet: Train derailments and crashes are common in Egypt, where the railway system has a history of mismanagement and poor maintenance of equipment. In recent years, the government has announced modernization initiatives.

entries.title: Floods bring rare relief to U.S. Southwest reservoirs as Lake Powell rises 20 feet
entries.snippet: Storms in late October and early November sent torrents of water through normally small or dry creeks that overflowed their banks and flooded local communities.

entries.title: Israel's president formally gives Eisenkot the first chance to form the next government
entries.snippet: The announcement doesn't guarantee that Eisenkot, a former army chief, will become the next prime minister. He has up to six weeks to form a coalition government by securing alliances, a daunting challenge because the Oct. 27 election gave neither his bloc nor Netanyahu's a clear

entries.title: What is Diwali, the Festival of Lights, and how is it celebrated?
entries.snippet: The festival follows the Hindu lunar calendar, typically falling in late October or early November. This year, Diwali falls on Nov. 8.

entries.title: Sen. Chris Murphy's stroke at 53 highlights a trend: Strokes among younger adults have risen
entries.snippet: Researchers found that the stroke incidence rate among adults from 1993-94 nearly doubled in 2020, jumping from 33.90 cases per 100,000 people to 62.18 cases.

entries.title: Trump says he's asked UFC's Dana White to be his press secretary
entries.snippet: Trump's social media post about the offer came as his White House is in a period of major transition and struggling with his party's deep losses in Tuesday's midterm elections.

entries.title: Israel's president taps opposition candidate Eisenkot to form a government, in setback for Netanyahu
entries.snippet: Neither Eisenkot nor Netanyahu won a clear majority in the vote. But in marathon discussions with the president this week, representatives from most of Israel's main parties recommended Eisenkot be tasked with assembling a new government.

entries.title: Melania Trump and LSU announce a scholarship program for students who were in foster care
entries.snippet: Trump and LSU secured more than $7 million in private donations to create an endowment fund for the scholarships, the White House said.

entries.title: Judge wants former U.S. attorney to investigate whether the government misled her in Trump golf case
entries.snippet: The administration plans to close the East Potomac Golf Course and park on Nov. 15 with the intention of constructing a "World Class, championship-level golf course that is capable of hosting major events."

entries.title: With an ode to mate, Pope Leo urges faithful in Uruguay to build bridges of fraternity and faith
entries.snippet: More than 30,000 people — many from Uruguay but also from neighboring Argentina and Brazil — had registered in advance to attend the service. The Vatican said Saturday that another 10,000 had attended, despite the morning rain.

entries.title: Scott Colom and Black Mississippians stand on the cusp of Senate history as vote count stretches on
entries.snippet: The state is still tallying ballots that could make Colom the first Black senator from this Deep South state since post-Civil War Reconstruction.

entries.title: In his words: Stephen Miller is an immigration hardliner and a bombastic critic of Democrats
entries.snippet: An outspoken defender of President Donald Trump's most far-reaching goals to remake government going back to his 2016 run for president, Miller is known for his harsh language and unapologetic bombast.

entries.title: DW
entries.snippet: News, Analysis and Service from Germany and Europe - in 30 Languages

entries.title: Iran: Trump says strikes unlikely if peace talks keep moving
entries.snippet: After weeks of rumors that the US and Israel were preparing new strikes on Iran, President Donald Trump said it was "highly unlikely" that he would order a new escalation as the Iranians "want to make a deal so badly."

entries.title: Germany news: Merz to nominate Aigner for president
entries.snippet: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz announced that he will nominate Ilse Aigner for federal president, paving the way for her to be the first woman to hold the office. DW has more.

entries.title: Many killed after migrant boat sinks off Senegal
entries.snippet: The incident occurred near Kebemer off the coast of northwestern Senegal. Authorities on El Hierro in the Canary Islands have declared an emergency after a marked increase in migrant boat arrivals.

entries.title: South Africa elections: ANC marks its worst-ever performance
entries.snippet: The African National Congress, the party of late Nobel Prize winner Nelson Mandela, slumped to its worst-ever result in South Africa's municipal election. The voters blame the ANC for water and electricity shortages.

entries.title: Egypt train crash leaves several dead, over 100 injured
entries.snippet: A train derailed after colliding with another train south of Cairo, with authorities confirming several deaths and saying more than 100 passengers were injured. Over 50 ambulances were deployed to the scene.

entries.title: Israel: Eisenkot officially tasked with forming a government
entries.snippet: Israeli President Isaac Herzog tasked Gadi Eisenkot with the right of trying to form a government. The opposition leader's way to replacing Benjamin Netanyahu as prime minister is full of political challenges.

entries.title: Iran: US strikes ship after Hormuz blockade breach
entries.snippet: The US military said a vessel trying to leave an Iranian port was hit due to the naval blockade on the country. On its part, Iran said three "non compliant" oil tankers caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz.

entries.title: Gaza: Rains add misery to humanitarian catastrophe
entries.snippet: With most homes damaged or destroyed by the war, Gazans are facing worsening humanitarian conditions due to heavy rain.

entries.title: 'Never Again!': Holocaust remembrance under pressure
entries.snippet: Only a few Holocaust survivors remain who can share their stories firsthand. Meanwhile, voices calling for an end to what they describe as a "cult of guilt" are growing louder. How can Holocaust remembrance survive?

entries.title: Poland begins two days of mourning over Krakow shooting
entries.snippet: Polish authorities have opened a terror probe after the shooting on Krakow's Main Square. Police confirmed that the bodies found at the suspect's home were those of his parents and sister.

entries.title: India: Delhi chokes on most polluted Diwali eve in 10 years
entries.snippet: Delhi was ranked as the world's most polluted major city on the eve of Diwali. Delhi's air pollution is expected to get worse in the coming days.

entries.title: As COP31 Antalya kicks off, can world move beyond big promises?
entries.snippet: Droughts, floods and extreme heat are upping the pressure on delegates at the UN climate talks in Antalya, Turkey. Can countries move beyond pledges to concrete action?

entries.title: Poland: Gunman kills 6 in Krakow main square, police say
entries.snippet: A suspect who fired from a car killed at least six people, including a British tourist, in Krakow's main market square. Officials said the man was fascinated with "radical" and "far-right" ideologies.

entries.title: Ebola: Why is there still no vaccine?
entries.snippet: Ebola has been known about for decades, but there is still no vaccine against the Bundibugyo strain of the virus causing the current outbreak. New research raises hopes of protection against the various types of Ebola.

entries.title: Israeli president tasks Gadi Eisenkot with forming government
entries.snippet: President Isaac Herzog has picked former Israeli military chief Gadi Eisenkot, leader of an anti-Netanyahu alliance, to take the first shot at trying to form a government. Tricky coalition talks are expected.

entries.title: Trump offers White House press secretary role to Dana White
entries.snippet: US President Donald Trump has offered the White House press secretary job to Dana White, the chief executive of the Ultimate Fighting Championship. White has neither formally accepted nor turned down the invitation.

entries.title: France sees new round of Yellow Vest, student protests
entries.snippet: Although fewer protesters turned out in comparison with previous weeks, several cities saw clashes between police and demonstrators.

entries.title: Armenia's selective prosecution: A threat to EU relations?
entries.snippet: While Brussels has refrained from harsh criticism, Armenian civil society has warned of selective justice against opposition figures. Could the EU's pragmatic stance risk repeating past mistakes?

entries.title: More than 40,000 gather as Pope Leo XIV celebrates Mass in Uruguay
entries.snippet: Leo celebrated the first Mass of his South America tour less than a month after undergoing cancer surgery. He is seeking to raise interest in the Catholic Church in Uruguay, South America's most secular country.
